Notey's World · Contextual helper

Pico, your guitar friend

Pico is a small guitar-pick friend who stands next to the strings. It cheers when the guitar is heard, looks kind when a note is off, and steps in with a hint or a short lesson when a player keeps missing the same note.

Figma file Figma prototype Video walkthrough

What Pico does

One character, three jobs
Buddy · Always on

A living buddy

Pico follows the player through every performance. It cheers when things go well and grows worried when they don't, reacting to what the player plays in real time. It never interrupts the game and it never talks.

Helper · Automatic

Help when it's needed

When certain circumstances are met, Pico steps in during the gameplay with a visual tip or an offer of help. Short cues that the player can follow or ignore, with nothing blocking the game.

Helper · Player's choice

A permanent Help button

Pico is always there to be tapped. On the player's demand it launches a dedicated lesson or a troubleshooting guide, so help is always one tap away and never forced on the player.

Design notes

Principles behind the prototype

Automatic, manual or both?

Both. Pico is always there to be tapped, and it also steps in by itself when the player seems to need it. The two never compete: what happens automatically can only suggest or point, and the player alone decides to open a lesson. Help is offered, never imposed.

Reading the situation, not the player

The signals come from the game's own sound detection: whether notes are hit, whether the same note keeps failing, and whether anything is heard at all. A wrong note and a silent room are different problems, so they get different help: a musical hint for the first, a setup check for the second. Every threshold is a starting estimate, listed in the rules and thresholds below.

Quiet by default, never patronising

Help grows only as fast as the need. A reaction comes first, a visual cue after repeated misses, an offer of help after that, and a lesson only on request. Cues are pictures or a few words, are about the note and never about the player, and are not repeated once ignored. Pico behaves like a friend sitting next to the player, not a teacher grading the performance.

The player stays in control

Every cue expires on its own or can be waved away with a single tap, and nothing needs a close button. Pico can be tapped at any moment, so help can be revisited as often as wanted at no cost. Declining returns to play with a short countdown, so the player is never dropped back into a moving game.

Momentum comes first

The game never pauses by itself. Cues sit outside the note lane and the controls, stay short, and leave without being asked. The only pause is the one the player chooses, and a lesson is built to be left quickly: it asks for one correct play and then hands the game back.

Honest when it can't hear

Audio recognition will sometimes be uncertain, and Pico never pretends otherwise. It says what it notices, not what the player did wrong, and it separates "I heard something" from "I heard nothing". When nothing is heard the help is about the setup, with simple checks, and it never blames the player's playing. As soon as a note is heard, the help moves to the state that fits it.

Unblocked is earned by playing

Help is judged by what happens next, not by a button saying "got it". A single clean hit can be luck, so two clean plays in a row count as unblocked, and only then does Pico step back to its usual role. If the player is still missing, Pico stays available without escalating.

Easy to turn off

A PICO card in Settings > Gameplay switches Pico Off or On, with On by default. Off removes it completely, and the player brings it back from the same place. The switch lives only in Settings, so it can't be flipped by accident during play.

Rules and thresholds

Every number below is a starting estimate, not a validated value. They are meant to be tested and confirmed against real session duration and real player behaviour, then tuned.

Correct hit

Pico cheers on every correct hit.

1st miss

Pico gives a kind tilt.

2 misses in a row

Pico looks worried.

Visual hint

After 2 consecutive misses, a ring and light mark the next note about 2 seconds before it reaches the strike line. Hints are at least 15 seconds apart.

"Stuck? I can help!"

Appears after 3 visual hints without a correct hit.

"I can't hear you!"

Appears after 3 missed notes with no sound detected.

Balloon duration

Balloons stay about 6 seconds, then fade.

Tutoring/troubleshooting modal timeout

The modal opens on the fretboard and switches to No sound after about 10 seconds with no microphone input. After "I can't hear you!" it opens directly on No sound.

Unblocking

2 clean plays in a row count as unblocked.
